title: Brag
subtitle: A beginner's guide to /brag, the free AI agent skill that turns a project you built into a short launch video with music, motion and ready-to-post captions.
info: Free and open source. You pay only for your AI agent (e.g. a Claude plan).
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, opencode and other agents

sections.p: You build an app or website with AI. Now you want to show it off on X, LinkedIn or Instagram. /brag is a skill you add to your AI coding agent. Type /brag inside your project and the agent reads your code, plans a story, and makes a 15 to 25 second launch video with a soundtrack, sound effects and a short caption to post with it.
Think of it as a video editor that already understands your product, because it read the code instead of watching a screen recording.

table: Plans the story, then hands a brief to Hyperframes (a video tool by HeyGen), which builds and renders the video
Any AI model; also needed for voiceover
The agent builds the whole video itself. No Hyperframes, no bundled assets
Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.2 (picked automatically on these)

bullets: Good fit: vibe coders, indie makers and founders who want a polished launch clip for a project they built.
Good fit: creators who show off AI-built apps on Reels, Shorts or X. It supports vertical 9:16 videos.
Not for: editing your own camera footage or talking-head reels. It makes videos about a code project.
Don't want to install anything? The makers also run letsbrag.app: paste your site's link and it makes the video for you.
An AI agent that supports skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode and similar.
FFmpeg installed and available in your terminal (it creates the video file).
Hyperframes CLI for the full /brag: check it with npx hyperframes doctor.
A project folder with your website or app code.

sections.code:
codex plugin marketplace add latent-spaces/brag
codex plugin add brag@brag

sections.h2: Any other agent (Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, opencode...)

sections.code:
npx skills add https://github.com/latent-spaces/brag --skill brag

# only the lighter version:
npx skills add https://github.com/latent-spaces/brag --skill brag-slim

sections.small: Add <font name='Courier'>-g</font> to the npx command to install it for every project. Restart your agent after installing. Windows users who copy the repo manually need Git symlinks enabled, or should copy the <font name='Courier'>skills/brag/</font> folder by hand.

sections.p: Open your project in your agent and type:

sections.code:
/brag --tone "fake Series A launch from 2016"
/brag --format vertical          # 9:16 for Reels, Shorts, TikTok
/brag --voice                    # add an AI voiceover (full /brag only)

sections.p: When it finishes you get a <font name='Courier'>brag-output/</font> folder:

table: The best frame, used as the thumbnail
1 to 3 sentences ready to post with the video
The story plan and storyboard, so you can ask for changes
Style: polished, yc-parody, chaotic, deadpan, cinematic, app-store, or your own words
The product name shown in the video

sections.callout: The video is meant to be posted publicly. The skill is told to skip secrets, keys, .env files and real customer data, and to swap in made-up names if your app shows personal data. Still watch the whole video and read the caption before posting, especially for client or work projects.
sections.title: Check before you post

bullets: It uses your AI usage. Reading the code, planning and building a video takes many agent steps, so expect it to use a good share of your plan or API credits.
Rendering needs FFmpeg (and Hyperframes for the full version). Most install problems come from these, so run npx hyperframes doctor first.
Music is licensed. The bundled track is from ende.app under CC BY 4.0 and the sound effects are from Kenney. CC BY means giving credit when you post.
Actively maintained: updated in November 2026, with tens of thousands of GitHub stars.
